description.value: La Taquería is a full-service Mexican restaurant in Burnaby's Brentwood area, one of three distinct concepts operated by the same restaurant group. It offers a culinary-focused dining experience with cocktails, full table service, and an expansive menu of traditional dishes — from street-style tacos and quesabirria to enchiladas and birriamen. Touring cyclists stopping in the Brentwood corridor will find a sit-down meal with both indoor and outdoor seating and vegetarian and vegan options.

bike_parking_detail: 2 racks within 100m: stands (22 spaces, covered) at 56m; rack (3 spaces) at 77m. Total: 25 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms La Taquería Restaurant is open and operating at 4580 Brentwood (Unit 1210), Burnaby — matching the OSM record, though the street name differs (OSM: Lougheed Highway; website: Brentwood Blvd), likely reflecting the Brentwood Town Centre mall address vs. the official highway address. OSM tags diet:vegan=yes and diet:vegetarian=yes are corroborated by multiple plant-based taco, burrito, and specialty options visible in the website menu. No cyclist-specific amenities (bike parking, Wi-Fi, water refill, etc.) are mentioned anywhere in the website content or OSM tags beyond what is noted.
concerns: Address discrepancy: OSM lists the street as 'Lougheed Highway' but the website uses 'Brentwood Blvd' (as in '4580 Brentwood Blvd, unit 1210'). These likely refer to the same Brentwood Town Centre mall location, but the canonical street address should be verified.
No phone number present in either OSM or website content.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, open, publicly accessible restaurant confirmed by website content with active menu and online ordering. A useful food and drink stop for cyclists on the Lougheed corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: This location is one of three concepts under the lataqueria.com umbrella. The other two — Pinche Taco Shop (367 Seymour St, Vancouver) and Comedor (2450 Yukon St) — are separate locations and would require their own OSM records.
